why: One route, two transports. ask-core's makeIntelAsk posts with a plain fetch and a
static key (`mla ask`); the CLI's makeIntelAskFromCli posts through http.ts so the
MCP server carries a user-token bearer and its reactive refresh. The TRANSPORT has
to differ. The BODY must not, and this file is the one artifact both of them are
measured against, so a field added to one and forgotten in the other is a red test
in two suites instead of a silent divergence on the wire.
Read by:
packages/ask-core/ask_modes.test.js       (node --test)
packages/cli/test/lib/egress-ownership.spec.ts (jest)
`wire` is compared as a STRING, not a deep-equal, so key ORDER is pinned too: the
serialized body is what actually leaves the process.
The question carries a credential and a deep path on purpose. Both builders redact
at the `retrieval` bar, so the fixture proves the secret is gone AND that the path
which makes the question retrievable survived. A builder that redacted at `full`
would pass a shape check and fail here.
`builder` is the part of the body that is NOT a property of the call. The metering
actor is bound when the closure is constructed (ask-core takes it as `userId` in its
deps; the CLI reads it off `cfg.actorUserId`), because the mode handlers that invoke
the closure never see an operator. Both suites must bind this id before comparing
against `wire`, which is exactly the point: it pins the id's PLACE in the body, so a
builder that started sending it per-call, or stopped sending it at all, goes red.
